You have recently detected a suspicious pattern in your organization’s Google Drive usage. Several users have shared sensitive documents externally, potentially breaching your company’s data-security policy. You need to identify the users responsible and the scope of the unauthorized sharing. What should you do?

options.text: Create an activity rule in the Security Center to alert you of future external sharing events.
Use the security health page to identify misconfigured sharing settings in Drive.
Review the organization's sharing policies in the Admin console, and update the policies to prevent external sharing.
Use the security investigation tool to analyze Drive logs and identify the users.

questions.explanation:
The security investigation tool can search and analyze Drive log events to review historical Google Drive activity, including sharing-related actions, so administrators can identify the responsible users and assess the extent of unauthorized sharing.

**Learn more:** [Drive log events — Google Workspace Admin Help](https://support.google.com/a/answer/4579696) · [Data sources for the security investigation tool — Google Workspace Admin Help](https://support.google.com/a/answer/11482175)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An employee in your organization might be sharing confidential documents with unauthorized external parties. You need to quickly find out whether any sensitive information has leaked. What should you do?

options.text: Review the employee's Drive log events in the security investigation tool.
Create a custom report of the user's external sharing by using the security dashboard.
Review the employee's user log events within the security investigation tool.
Audit Drive access by using the Admin SDK Reports API.

questions.explanation:
Drive log events record user activity in Google Drive. The security investigation tool can investigate files shared outside the organization by using the Drive log events data source and filtering for externally shared visibility, allowing the administrator to identify potentially leaked sensitive documents.

**Learn more:** [Drive log events — Google Workspace Admin Help](https://support.google.com/a/answer/4579696) · [Data sources for the security investigation tool — Google Workspace Admin Help](https://support.google.com/a/answer/11482175)

questions.question: Your organization lets employees use their personal mobile devices to access their work email. You need to remove an employee’s work email data from their phone when they leave the organization. What should you do?

options.text: Set up basic mobile management on the devices.
Set up advanced mobile management on the devices.
Set up data protection rules to prevent data sharing externally.
Set up 2SV authentication on the devices.

questions.explanation:
Basic mobile management supports wiping a user’s work account from a mobile device, removing the work email and other account-associated organization data without requiring a full-device wipe.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set up basic mobile device management](https://support.google.com/a/answer/7400753)

questions.question: Your organization lets employees use their personal mobile devices to access their work email. You need to remove an employee’s work email data from their phone when they leave the organization. What should you do?

options.text: Redirect the acquired domain to Google’s MX records and add the account as a “send as” address.
Set up the acquired agency as a secondary domain from the Manage domains page.
Set up the acquired agency as a user alias domain from the Manage domains page.
Set up the acquired agency as a secondary domain and swap it to the primary domain.

questions.explanation:
A Google Workspace user alias domain gives every user an email address at both the primary domain and the alias domain, allowing them to send and receive email using either address. A secondary domain is intended for a separate set of users with their own accounts and mailboxes.

**Learn more:** [Add a user alias domain or secondary domain](https://support.google.com/a/answer/7502379) · [FAQ for multiple domains](https://support.google.com/a/answer/175747)

A user has intermittent trouble accessing their Gmail inbox. At times Gmail loads slowly, while at other times the user receives undocumented error messages. You need to troubleshoot this recurring issue effectively. What should you do?

options.text: Check the Google Workspace Status Dashboard for any reported service disruptions.
Instruct the user to generate a HAR file the next time they experience slowness or an error.
Instruct the user to try to access Gmail from another device or network to see if the issue persists.
Instruct the user to clear their browser cache and cookies.

questions.explanation:

**Learn more:** [Fix common error messages in Gmail](https://support.google.com/mail/answer/7036382?hl=en)

Your organization has turned on Google Groups for Business so employees can create and manage their own email distribution lists and web forums. You must ensure users cannot join external Google Groups using their Google Workspace accounts, without disrupting internal group use. What should you do?

options.text: Set the setting for Google Groups for Business called Accessing groups from outside this organization to Private.
In Additional Google Services, turn Google Groups OFF at the root organizational unit.
Use the Directory API to change the settings of user-created groups to disable features that allow external users to access, view, or post on groups.
Set the setting for Google Groups for Business called Default for permission to view conversations to All organization users.

questions.explanation:
Setting **Accessing groups from outside this organization** to **Private** applies an organization-wide boundary that limits Google Groups access to people in the organization, while leaving internal Google Groups available. Google documents that the Private setting allows only people in the organization to access the organization’s groups in Google Groups.

**Learn more:** [Set organization-wide policies for using groups](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/groups/set-organization-wide-policies-for-using-groups?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company wants to enable single sign-on (SSO) so employees can access a newly acquired cloud-based marketing platform. The marketing-platform vendor has confirmed SAML 2.0 compatibility and supplied the required metadata. You need to simplify user access and centralize authentication through Google Workspace. What should you do?

options.text: Request an API key from the marketing platform vendor for SAML integration.
Enable two-factor authentication for all users to enhance security before implementing SSO.
Instruct employees to log in to the marketing platform using the Sign In with Google functionality.
Create a new SAML application in the Google Admin console.

questions.explanation:
A custom SAML application in the Google Admin console configures Google Workspace as the SAML identity provider and the marketing platform as the service provider, using the vendor’s SAML metadata. This lets employees authenticate with their managed Google Workspace identities for centralized SSO.

**Learn more:** [Zinc cloud app — Google Workspace Admin Help](https://support.google.com/a/answer/9002302?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for a global organization with offices in the United States and the European Union (EU). There is an organizational unit (OU) for employees in the United States and another OU for employees in the EU. Company regulations require you to ensure that users’ data is located in the same region as their physical office. What should you do?

options.text: Set the OU data location to No preference.
Turn on advanced settings and select Enable features that may process data across multiple regions.
Turn on advanced settings and select Disable features that may process data across multiple regions.
Set a data region policy for each region’s OU.

questions.explanation:
Google Workspace data regions can store covered data in a specified geographic location, including the United States or Europe (EU). For organizations that need different regions for different user populations, data region policies can be applied to organizational units; assign the United States policy to the US OU and the Europe policy to the EU OU.

**Learn more:** [Choose a geographic location for your data](https://support.google.com/a/answer/14310028?hl=en-GB) · [Compare data region features across Google Workspace editions](https://support.google.com/a/answer/14316863?hl=en-EN)

questions.domain: Managing security policies and access controls
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have received several reports of a suspicious email from someone impersonating your organization’s human resources department. The email asks employees to click a link to update their passwords. You want to remediate this sender’s emails. What should you do?

options.text: Use the security investigation tool to search for users who received the suspicious email, and select Mark message as phishing.
Use the security investigation tool to action the suspicious email and select Mark message as spam.
Create an activity rule to alert administrators to similar emails from that sender.
Notify all employees and request that they report this email as spam.

questions.explanation:
A credential-update message that impersonates a trusted internal department is a phishing attempt. The Google Workspace security investigation tool can identify users who received the message and take action on those messages, including marking them as phishing.

**Learn more:** [Take action based on search results](https://support.google.com/a/answer/9043224?hl=en) · [Investigate malicious email reports](https://support.google.com/a/answer/7581662?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization plans to introduce a bring-your-own-device (BYOD) program that lets users securely access corporate data on their personal devices. You must ensure that, if a user's personal device is lost or stolen, an unauthorized user cannot access corporate data, including data stored locally on the device. What should you do?

options.text: Enable advanced mobile management for all users in your organization participating in the BYOD program.
Allow only users who have devices with full device encryption to join the BYOD program.
Deploy device certificates for all users participating in the BYOD program.
Enable basic mobile management for users in your organization participating in the BYOD program, and require the users to complete an updated security training program.

questions.explanation:
Advanced mobile management provides controls to protect organizational data on personal mobile devices, including enforcing device encryption, restricting device features, and wiping data from a device. These controls address the risk of corporate data being accessed locally after a device is lost or stolen.

**Learn more:** [Set up advanced mobile management](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/devices/set-up-advanced-mobile-management?hl=en)

questions.question: A user in your organization reports that an internal event recipient is not receiving Calendar event invitations. You need to identify the cause of this issue. What should you do?

options.text: Check whether the business hours are set up in the event recipient's Calendar settings.
Check if Calendar service is turned off for the event creator
Check whether the Calendar event has more than 50 guests.
Check whether the event recipient has turned off their email notifications for new events in their Calendar settings.

questions.explanation:
A recipient who has disabled email notifications for new Calendar events may not receive invitation emails. Google Calendar’s invitation troubleshooting guidance directs administrators and users to verify that the guest has not turned off email notifications for new events.\
\
**Learn more:** [Google Calendar Help: Invite people to your Calendar event](https://support.google.com/calendar/answer/37161?hl=en-GB)

questions.question: A user in your organization reports that an internal event recipient is not receiving Calendar event invitations. You need to identify the cause of this issue. What should you do?

options.text: Add the acquired company’s domain name as a Secondary Domain, and create user accounts with the new domain name.
Add the acquired company's domain name as an alias domain.
Change the MX records of the old domain to point to the new domain.
Create a mail routing rule in the new domain to route messages addressed to the old domain.

questions.explanation:
A user alias domain automatically gives users an alternate email address at the added domain. Users can send and receive messages using either their primary-domain address or the corresponding alias-domain address. A secondary domain is intended for separate user accounts and mailboxes, rather than providing the same users with addresses at both domains.

**Learn more:** [Add a user alias domain or secondary domain](https://support.google.com/a/answer/7502379)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Several users in your organization report that they are not receiving Calendar invitations sent by a particular department. You confirmed that the invitations are being sent and that the sender’s logs contain no error messages. You want to troubleshoot the problem. What should you do?

options.text: Analyze the message headers of the sent invitations by using the Google Admin Toolbox to identify any delivery issues.
Verify that the senders in the specific department have the necessary permissions to share their calendars externally and send invitations outside of the organization.
Disable and re-enable the Calendar service for the affected users to refresh their connection.
Check the affected users’ Calendar settings to confirm whether they have accidentally blocked invitations from the specific department.

questions.explanation:
Calendar invitations are email messages, and message headers record the routing path and delivery-related details needed to identify delays or delivery failures. Google Workspace guidance recommends copying the full header into Google Admin Toolbox Messageheader to analyze the message’s route and determine where a delay occurred.

**Learn more:** [Trace an email with its full header](https://support.google.com/mail/answer/29436?hl=en) · [Troubleshoot message delivery with Email Log Search](https://support.google.com/a/answer/7513679?hl=en-GB)

questions.domain: Managing security policies and access controls
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company sends an internal newsletter containing sensitive information to every employee by email. You have observed unauthorized forwarding of this newsletter to external addresses, which could cause data leaks. To prevent this, you need a solution that automatically detects and blocks this forwarding while still permitting legitimate internal sharing. What should you do?

options.text: Add a banner to the newsletter that warns users that external sharing is prohibited.
Create a Gmail content compliance rule that targets the internal newsletter, identifying instances of external forwarding. Configure the rule to reject the message when such forwarding is detected
Develop an Apps Script project by using the Gmail API to scan sent emails for the newsletter content and external recipients. Automatically revoke access for violating users.
Create a content compliance rule to modify the newsletter subject line, adding a warning against external forwarding.

questions.explanation:
Gmail content compliance rules can identify messages by matching newsletter content and apply to outbound mail with external recipients. Configuring the matching rule to reject the message blocks delivery before it reaches the external recipient, while internal sharing is unaffected by the external-recipient scope.

**Learn more:** [Set up rules for advanced email content filtering](https://support.google.com/a/answer/1346934?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A department in your company needs access to the latest AI-powered capabilities in Google Workspace. You know Gemini provides advanced capabilities, and you must give the department immediate access to Gemini features while maintaining deployment control so corporate data is not available for human review. What should you do?

options.text: Enable Alpha features for the organization and assign Gemini licenses to all users.
Monitor Gemini adoption through the administrator console and wait for wider user adoption before assigning licenses.
Enable Gemini for the department's organizational unit and assign Gemini licenses to users in the department.
Enable Gemini for non-licensed users in that department so they have immediate access to the free service.

questions.explanation:
Gemini Advanced users with qualifying Google Workspace licenses receive enterprise-grade data protections: their content is not reviewed by humans or used to train generative AI models outside their domain without permission. Enabling Gemini for the department’s organizational unit scopes access to that department, and licensing its users provides the advanced Gemini capabilities. Users of the free additional service may have chats reviewed by humans, so that option does not satisfy the corporate-data requirement.

**Learn more:** [Turn the Gemini app on or off](https://support.google.com/a/answer/14571493) · [Gemini for Google Workspace FAQ](https://support.google.com/a/answer/14130944)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization wants to stop a group of users from signing in to Google Drive while traveling internationally for business.  
  
You have placed these users in an organizational unit (OU). You need to secure the users’ access to the Google Drive app to satisfy this requirement.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Disable Google Drive for users in the OU.
Define location-based access levels. Assign the levels to the Google Drive app for the OU.
Require 2-step verification (2SV) when users in the OU sign in.
Define user-based access levels. Assign the levels to the Google Drive app for the OU.

questions.explanation:
Google Workspace Context-Aware Access can control access to Workspace apps using context attributes, including location. A location-based access level assigned to Google Drive for the applicable OU blocks Drive access when users do not meet the permitted location condition.

**Learn more:** [About Context-Aware Access](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/security/about-context-aware-access?visit_id=639116142068727610-206888089&rd=1)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company supplies shared Chromebook workstations for employees to access sensitive company data. You must configure the devices so that no sensitive data is retained locally and browsing data is cleared after every use. What should you do?

options.text: Force ephemeral mode in Chrome. Disable offline access for sensitive Workspace apps like Docs, Sheets, and Drive.
Enable the Manage Guest Session functionality, and set the maximum user session length.
Force ephemeral mode in Chrome. Allow offline access for all Workspace apps with strict expiration times.
Disable offline access for all Workspace apps. Enable incognito mode for Chrome browsing sessions.

questions.explanation:
On ChromeOS, enforcing ephemeral users deletes local user data when a user signs out, preventing one user’s browsing and profile data from remaining for the next user. Offline Google Workspace access saves files or cached content on the device, so offline access for sensitive Docs, Sheets, and Drive services must be disabled to meet a no-local-storage requirement.

**Learn more:** [Allow private browsing](https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/9302896?hl=en) · [Use Google Drive files offline](https://support.google.com/drive/answer/2375012?co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop&hl=en-en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization stores credit card information in customer files. You need to implement a policy for your organization’s Google Drive data that prevents accidental external sharing of files containing credit card numbers. You also need to log any sharing incidents for reporting. What should you do?

options.text: Create a data loss prevention (DLP) rule that uses the predefined credit card number detector, sets the action to “block external sharing”, and enables the “Log event” option.
Enable Gmail content compliance, and create a rule to block email attachments containing credit card numbers from being sent to external recipients.
Implement a third-party data loss prevention solution to integrate with Drive and provide advanced content detection capabilities.
Configure a data retention policy to automatically delete files containing credit card numbers after a specified period.

questions.explanation:
A Google Drive data loss prevention (DLP) rule can use the predefined credit card number detector to identify sensitive content and apply the **Block external sharing** action. DLP detection and action events are recorded in Rule log events, providing an auditable record for reporting.

**Learn more:** [Create DLP for Drive rules and custom content detectors](https://support.google.com/a/answer/9655387) · [About DLP](https://support.google.com/a/answer/9646351)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An end user has thousands of files stored in Google Drive. Their files are well organized using Drive labels. You need to advise the end user how to quickly identify all files that are contracts. What should you do?

options.text: Advise the user to use the Google Drive API to search for files with the keyword “contracts”
Advise the user to search in Drive for files with the keyword “contracts”, and use the “modified by me” filter.
Advise the user to search for files that are labeled as “contracts”.
Advise the user to use the Investigation tool to search for files with the keyword “contracts” and updated by you.

questions.explanation:
Google Drive search options can find content with a specific Drive label. Selecting the **contracts** label returns accessible files to which that label is applied, making it the direct way to identify all contract files.

**Learn more:** [Apply labels to files in Google Drive](https://support.google.com/drive/answer/13495216?co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop&hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization’s IT department requires a dedicated auditor to oversee and validate activity in Google Vault. You must give the auditor complete read-only access to Vault retention policies and matters, while preventing the auditor from making changes or taking actions. What should you do?

options.text: Assign the super admin role to the auditor and remove all privileges except “View All Matters.”
Create a custom role with “View” privileges for Retention Policies and All Matters. Assign the role to the auditor.
Create a custom role with the “View All Matters” privilege and assign the role to the auditor.
Create a custom role with the “Manage Matters” privilege and assign the role to the auditor. Ensure the auditor is not assigned to any specific matters.

questions.explanation:
The Google Vault privileges “View Retention Policies” and “View All Matters” provide read-only visibility into all organization-wide retention rules and all matters, respectively. Neither privilege grants the ability to create, modify, close, delete, or otherwise manage Vault resources.

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An employee is departing your company and has many files stored in My Drive. Their manager needs to keep access to these files. You must offboard the departing employee’s Google Workspace account while ensuring the manager can still access the files and following Google-recommended practices. What should you do?

options.text: Use Google Vault to establish a retention policy for the organizational unit (OU) of the departing employee. Assign the Google Archived User license.
Instruct the departing employee to share their My Drive folder with the manager before leaving. Delete the Google Workspace account on the departing employee’s last day.
Download the departing employee’s Drive data by using Google Takeout. Upload the data to the manager’s Drive before deleting the departing employee’s Google Workspace account.
Transfer ownership of the departing employee’s files to the manager during the user deletion process.

questions.explanation:
Google Workspace administrators can transfer ownership of a user’s My Drive files to another active user when deleting the account. This retains the files in the organization and gives the manager continued access under their own account.

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization requires a purchase-approval application in which a user can enter information about the required purchase and submit it for management approval. options.text: Suggest that the organization develop an application internally with a database, a backend service for data retrieval, and a frontend service for the application’s user interface.
Suggest that the organization continue to approve requests manually until budget is available to use a third-party application provider.
Suggest the organization use AppSheet to create the application.
Suggest that the organization use AppScript to create forms linked to a Google Sheet to store the purchase data.

questions.explanation:
AppSheet is a no-code application development platform that enables business users to create and customize applications through an interactive interface. questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Today, your company signed up for Google Workspace Business Starter using an existing domain name. options.text: Run the Transfer tool to bring unmanaged users to your Workspace account.

questions.explanation:

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An employee with a Workspace Enterprise Standard license has been terminated from your organization. You need to ensure the former employee can no longer access their Workspace account while preserving the former employee’s documents for the manager and team.  
  
You want to minimize licensing costs. What should you do?

options.text: Delete the former employee’s Workspace account.
Suspend former employee’s Workspace account.
Reset the password of the former employee and keep their Workspace license active.
Switch the license type of the former employee’s Workspace account to an Archived User license.

questions.explanation:
An Archived User license blocks the former employee’s access while retaining their Google Workspace data. It is supported for Enterprise Standard and frees the active Enterprise Standard license for reassignment, unlike a suspended account, which is billed at the same rate as an active account.

**Learn more:** [Preserve data for users who leave your organization](https://support.google.com/vault/answer/2736622?hl=en) · [Google Workspace Archived User orders & cancellations](https://support.google.com/channelservices/answer/9398454?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization has recently deployed Google Workspace. options.text: Export the external contacts to a CSV file, upload the file to Google Drive, and instruct users to import to their My Contacts.

Create a CNAME record that maps your domain to “gmail.com.”

questions.question: Your company plans to begin using Google Workspace for email. Your domain has been verified through a third-party provider. You need to route email to Google Workspace. What should you do?

options.text: Search the sender’s email address by using Email Log Search. Identify the users that received the messages. Instruct them to mark them as spam in Gmail, delete the messages, and empty the trash.

Search for the sender’s email address by using the security investigation tool. Mark the messages as phishing. Add the sender’s email address to the Blocked senders list in the Spam, Phishing and Malware setting in Gmail to automatically reject future messages.

Collect a list of users who received the messages. Search the recipients’ email addresses in Google Vault. Export and download the malicious emails in PST file format. Add the sender’s email address to a quarantine list setting in Gmail to quarantine any future emails from the sender.
Search for the sender’s email address by using the security investigation tool. Delete the messages. Turn on the safety options for spoofing and authentication protection in Gmail settings.

questions.explanation:
The Google Workspace security investigation tool supports investigating Gmail messages, identifying affected recipients, and removing malicious messages from user inboxes. Gmail’s spoofing and authentication protection is designed to help protect against messages impersonating people in the organization, addressing the apparent HR spoofing attack and reducing recurrence.

**Learn more:** [Data sources for the security investigation tool](https://support.google.com/a/answer/11482175) · [View alert details](https://support.google.com/a/answer/9104586)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company is migrating to Google Workspace from legacy communication and collaboration applications. User accounts are managed in Active Directory and synchronized to Google Workspace using Google Cloud Directory Sync (GCDS). Your company is implementing a new security policy for all accounts that requires complex passwords. Passwords must be at least 20 characters long and include 3 symbols, 4 numbers, and 2 capital letters.  
  
You need to enforce the new password policy in Google Workspace. What should you do?

options.text: Share the instructions for changing a Google account password with your users. Monitor password strength in the Google Admin console as users change their passwords.
Enable strong password enforcement and require a minimum length of 20 characters at the top-level organizational unit.
Create a password policy in Active Directory. Install Password Sync on the global catalog servers for Active Directory and require a password change for your users.
Create a password policy in Active Directory. Enable password synchronization in GCDS.

questions.explanation:
Active Directory should be the authoritative location for enforcing the password policy when it manages user accounts. Password Sync sends each Active Directory password change to the associated managed Google account, allowing the Active Directory policy to govern the synchronized Google Workspace password. Google Workspace password controls can require a minimum length and reject weak passwords, but they do not express the specified counts of symbols, numbers, and uppercase letters.

**Learn more:** [Overview: Password Sync](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/users/overview-password-sync?rd=1&visit_id=639166856123147655-238624255) · [What is synced?](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/users/what-is-synced?rd=1&visit_id=639188815732810355-3592158031)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],The legal department at your organization is handling a time-critical merger and acquisition (M&A) deal. It urgently needs access to particular email communications from an employee who is currently on leave. The organization’s current retention policy is indefinite. You need to retrieve the needed emails for the legal department in a way that preserves data privacy. What should you do?

options.text: Instruct the IT department to directly access and forward the relevant emails to the legal department.
Temporarily grant the legal department access to the employee’s email account with a restricted scope that is limited to the M&A-related emails.
Ask a colleague with delegate access to the employee's mailbox to identify and forward the relevant emails to the legal department.
Use Google Vault to create a matter specific to the M&A deal. Search for relevant emails within the employee's mailbox. Export and share relevant emails with your legal department.

questions.explanation:
Google Vault supports eDiscovery by using a matter to organize a legal project, search Gmail data for a specific account and relevant criteria, and export copies of only the matching results. This provides a controlled, auditable way to provide the legal department with the required communications without granting direct access to the employee’s mailbox.

**Learn more:** [Get started with Vault search & export](https://support.google.com/vault/answer/6161352?hl=en-GB) · [Export data from Vault](https://support.google.com/vault/answer/2473458?hl=en)

questions.question: An employee at your company told you they could access a Google Drive label used to identify confidential information. This unintended access creates a significant security risk. You must immediately limit access to this label and prevent any future misuse. What should you do?

options.text: Set the label permissions to Restricted access.
Set the label permissions to can apply labels and set values.
Disable the label for Drive.
Create and apply a policy that restricts sharing access for files associated with this label in Drive.

questions.explanation:
Restricted access limits a classification label so that only the users and groups explicitly specified can view or apply it. This directly prevents unauthorized users from accessing or misusing a confidential-information label.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create classification labels for your organization](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/security/create-classification-labels-for-your-organization)

questions.question: An employee at your company told you they could access a Google Drive label used to identify confidential information. This unintended access creates a significant security risk. You must immediately limit access to this label and prevent any future misuse. What should you do?

options.text: Create data loss prevention (DLP) rules for Drive. Configure the rules to apply Drive labels based on content.
Apply Drive labels based on content. Use Google Vault to create retention rules based on Drive labels, ensuring that data is kept for the required duration.
Implement a third-party data governance tool that integrates with Drive and provides advanced classification capabilities.
Add users into organizational units (OUs). Configure default file classification in Drive for the desired OUs.

questions.explanation:
Google Workspace DLP for Drive rules scan file content for sensitive-data detectors and can apply an existing Drive label automatically to matching files. This provides native, automated, content-based classification for files in Drive.

**Learn more:** [Create DLP for Drive rules and custom content detectors](https://support.google.com/a/answer/9655387)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],The compliance team has noticed that employees in your organization frequently reset their passwords and is worried about account hijacking. You need to create a solution that notifies the compliance team whenever a user changes or resets their password. What should you do?

options.text: Create and enforce a new password policy for all users in your organization.
Move all compliance team members into a separate organizational unit (OU). Create and enforce a new password policy for the members of this OU.
Create an activity rule that is triggered by the User’s password changed event. Add compliance team members as email recipients.
Create a new alert by using user log events. Check that the challenge type is “Password”, and add the compliance team as email recipients.

questions.explanation:
Google Workspace’s “User’s password changed” system-defined rule detects password changes in the organization and can send email notifications when its conditions are met. Configuring an activity rule for that event and adding compliance-team members as recipients provides the required notification.

**Learn more:** [View and edit system-defined rules — Google Workspace Admin Help](https://support.google.com/a/answer/3230421?hl=en-gb&ref_topic=11399553) · [Create and manage activity rules — Google Workspace Admin Help](https://support.google.com/a/answer/9275024?hl=en-419)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],The human resources department informed you that a legal investigation has begun for an employee in the finance department. You must ensure that this employee's Google Drive data is retained for at least one year and is not deleted by the user or through other means. The Google Vault default retention rules for Drive are configured for five years. What should you do?

options.text: Create a hold in Vault for the employee's Drive.
Place the employee into a separate organizational unit (OU). Create a custom one-year retention rule for this OU.
Change the Vault default retention rule to one year instead of five.
Confirm that the Vault default retention rule is set for five years.

questions.explanation:
A Google Vault hold on an individual employee’s Drive preserves the covered data indefinitely and takes precedence over default and custom retention rules. Files deleted by the user remain available in Vault rather than being purged, meeting the legal-preservation requirement for at least one year.

**Learn more:** [Place Drive, Meet, and Sites data on hold - Google Vault Help](https://support.google.com/vault/answer/7657464?hl=en) · [Manage retention rules and holds - Google Vault Help](https://support.google.com/vault/answer/3374023?hl=en)

You manage your organization’s buildings and resources. You need to create several conference rooms, each with a capacity of 10 people, a whiteboard and projector, and wheelchair accessibility. You want to make this process efficient. What should you do?

options.text: Automate room creation by using a third-party app from the Google Workspace Marketplace.
Create a CSV file and add all resources. Write a script using the Workspace API to reference the CSV file and create all the resources.
Create each conference room individually in the Google Admin console. Add the features for each room.
Use the Google Admin console to bulk upload the rooms. Create a resource with the specified features and apply the features to that resource.

questions.explanation:
Google Workspace lets administrators bulk-upload Calendar resources from a CSV in the Admin console. Resource features can represent equipment and accessibility attributes, allowing the required whiteboard, projector, and wheelchair-accessible room configuration to be applied consistently across multiple conference-room resources.

questions.domain: Managing security policies and access controls
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has a globally distributed remote workforce. You need to ensure that every team member follows the company’s data-security policies and accesses only authorized systems according to their location and role. What should you do?

options.text: Set up and mandate the use of a company-wide VPN for all remote access.
Create and enforce data loss prevention (DLP) rules to control data sharing
Configure access control policies with conditional access
Implement two-factor authentication for all remote team members

questions.explanation:
Conditional access policies enforce access decisions using signals such as user identity, group or role assignment, and network location. They can grant, restrict, or block access to resources so that only appropriately authorized users can access systems from permitted locations.

**Learn more:** [Build Conditional Access policies in Microsoft Entra](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-conditional-access-policies) · [Conditional Access — Block access by location](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-block-by-location)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization is rolling out a new Gmail-based customer support process. You need a cost-effective solution that lets external customers email support requests to the customer support team. The requests must be distributed evenly among the customer support agents. What should you do?

options.text: Create a Google Group, enable collaborative inbox settings, set posting permissions to “Anyone on the web”, and add the customer support agents as group members.
Use delegated access for a specific email address that represents the customer support group, and add the customer support team as delegates for that email address.
Create a Google Group, add the support agents to the group, and set the posting permissions to “Public.”
Set up an inbox for the customer support team. Provide the login credentials to the customer support team.

questions.explanation:
A Google Group configured as a Collaborative Inbox lets group members take and assign conversations to other members, which supports distributing support requests across agents. Setting posting permissions to allow anyone on the web lets external customers email the support group address. [Make a group a Collaborative Inbox](https://support.google.com/a/users/answer/10375787?hl=en)

**Learn more:** [Make a group a Collaborative Inbox](https://support.google.com/a/users/answer/10375787?hl=en) · [Take & assign conversations](https://support.google.com/groups/answer/2467048?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company recently migrated from an on-premises email solution to Google Workspace and has successfully added and verified the new primary domain. During a transitional period, it must still receive email sent to the former on-premises email server. Ensure that email addressed to the former domain continues to be delivered to the on-premises server, even though Google Workspace is now the primary email system. What should you do?

options.text: Configure MX records for the former domain to point to your on-premises email servers.
Add the former domain as a secondary domain in your Google Workspace settings and verity the domain.
Add the former domain as a domain alias for the primary domain.
Adjust the TTL (Time-to-Live) for the former domain to ensure a smooth transition.

questions.explanation: MX records specify the mail servers that receive email for a domain. Keeping the former domain’s MX records pointed at the on-premises email servers ensures that messages sent to that domain continue to be delivered there during the transition.

questions.question: You are investigating a possible data breach. You need to identify which devices are accessing corporate data and the applications in use. What should you do?

options.text: Analyze the audit log in the Admin console for device and application activity.
Analyze the security investigation tool to access device log data.
Analyze the Google Workspace reporting section of the Admin console.
Analyze the User Accounts section in the Google Admin console.

questions.explanation:
The Google Workspace security investigation tool provides device log data that gives a clear view of the devices and applications used to access organizational data.\
\
**Learn more:** [About the security center](https://support.google.com/a/answer/7492003?hl=en-au) · [Data sources for the security investigation tool](https://support.google.com/a/answer/11482175?hl=en-EN)

questions.question: You are investigating a possible data breach. You need to identify which devices are accessing corporate data and the applications in use. What should you do?

options.text: Add terramearth.com as a primary, secondary, or alias domain in Google Workspace. Update the Mail Exchange (MX) records with your domain registrar to direct mail flow to Google’s mail servers.
Establish a Transport Layer Security (TLS) connection between your company’s existing mail servers and Google’s mail servers
Configure an email address in Google Workspace to capture emails sent to unverified domains, including terramearth.com.
Create a domain alias for terramearth.com in Google Workspace. Configure email forwarding to redirect emails to the new Google Workspace accounts.

questions.explanation:
A domain must be added to Google Workspace as an appropriate domain type and have its DNS MX records directed to Google’s mail servers so external senders can deliver messages for that domain to Gmail. Google’s setup guidance requires updating the domain’s MX record and activating Gmail for the domain.

**Learn more:** [Set up MX records for Google Workspace](https://support.google.com/a/answer/6156494?hl=en-to) · [Add a user alias domain or secondary domain](https://support.google.com/a/answer/7502379?hl=en-AU)

questions.question: Your company recently purchased a new domain name for corporate email addresses. However, certain Google Workspace features are unavailable because the domain has not been verified. You need to verify the domain. What should you do?

options.text: Contact Google support and request manual verification.
Request a TXT record be added to the DNS zone by your domain registrar.
Purchase an SSL certificate for your domain.
Add an MX record to your DNS zone that points to Google Workspace.

questions.explanation: Google Workspace verifies domain ownership by having the domain’s DNS host publish a Google-provided TXT verification record. The record is added to the domain’s DNS zone, typically through the domain registrar or DNS provider.

questions.question: Your company recently purchased a new domain name for corporate email addresses. However, certain Google Workspace features are unavailable because the domain has not been verified. You need to verify the domain. What should you do?

options.text: Configure the Drive sharing options for the domain to internal only.
Restrict the Drive sharing options for the domain to allowlisted domains.
Create a Drive DLP rule, and use the sensitive internal Project name as the detector.
Turn off the Drive sharing setting from the Team dashboard.

questions.explanation:
A Google Drive DLP rule using a custom detector for the internal project name can identify files related to that project and apply the **Block external sharing** action. This preserves external sharing for other, non-sensitive content while ensuring matching project data remains internal.

**Learn more:** [Create DLP for Drive rules and custom content detectors](https://support.google.com/a/answer/9655387?hl=en-na)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You observe an increase in support cases involving the Chrome browser across your organization. You suspect a possible outage or service disruption affecting Chrome browser. You need to find out whether any information has been released about the issue and whether projected resolution timelines are available. What should you do first?

options.text: Use the Help Assistant within the Google Admin console to identify if there was a recent outage
Collect a HAR file and use the Google Admin Toolbox to identify potential failures.
Log a case with Chrome Enterprise support.
Review the Google Workspace Status Dashboard

questions.explanation:
The Google Workspace Status Dashboard publishes current and historical status for Chrome Browser, including service disruptions and outages. Its incident entries provide the known symptoms, mitigation status, and the timing of the next planned update, making it the appropriate initial source for outage information and projected updates.

**Learn more:** [Google Workspace Status Dashboard](https://www.google.com/appsstatus/dashboard/summary) · [Associate Google Workspace Administrator Exam Guide](https://services.google.com/fh/files/misc/associate_google_workspace_administrator_exam_guide_english.pdf)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your security team is concerned that disgruntled employees could download large quantities of intellectual property. You need to automatically send a notification when any user downloads more than 500 files from Google Drive during a one-hour period. What should you do?

options.text: Configure a Data Loss Prevention (DLP) rule for Drive.
Use the alert center to review Drive audit logs for instances where users download a large number of files.
Create an activity rule in the security investigation tool to monitor Drive download events. Set a threshold to trigger an alert.
Set up an alert within Google Cloud Monitoring to track the number of Drive API calls and trigger a notification when a user makes an excessive number of download requests.

questions.explanation:
Google Workspace activity rules can continuously evaluate Drive log-event searches and trigger alerts or notifications when the event frequency exceeds a configured threshold within a specified timeframe. A Drive download event filter with a one-hour threshold is the appropriate automated detection mechanism.

**Learn more:** [Create and manage activity rules](https://support.google.com/a/answer/9275024) · [Drive log events](https://support.google.com/a/answer/4579696)

questions.domain: Managing user accounts, domains, and Directory
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization has acquired a small agency with only five users. You need to create user accounts for these new employees. The agency users must retain their original email addresses. You have added the agency’s domain as a secondary domain. What should you do?

options.text: Manually create users from the Admin console. When creating the user account, choose the agency domain to be used for the email address.
Use the Directory API to automatically create the user accounts.
Bulk upload all users using a CSV file.
Use Google Cloud Directory Sync (GCDS) to sync users from an existing directory.

questions.explanation:
A Google Workspace secondary domain can have its own set of users with email addresses and mailboxes in that domain. When an administrator manually adds a user in the Admin console, they can select the secondary domain for the user’s primary email address, preserving the agency address.

**Learn more:** [Add a user alias domain or secondary domain](https://support.google.com/a/answer/7502379?hl=en-AU) · [Add an account for a new user](https://support.google.com/a/answer/33310?hl=)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A user who accesses sensitive data repeatedly has trouble opening certain Google Drive files from their laptop through the Chrome browser. When you contact Google Support, the support representative requests an HTTP archive (HAR) recording for review. You must share logs with Google Support while preserving data privacy. What should you do?

options.text: Open the HAR file in a text editor and delete sensitive information. Upload the HAR file to Google Drive and share the file only with the Google support representative
Ask the Google support representative for access to a Google Drive folder used by the Google support team. Upload the HAR file.
Share your screen with the Google support representative so they can view the file without having a copy of the file.
Upload the HAR file to Google Drive and share the file with the Google support representative.

questions.explanation:
HAR files can include the content of pages downloaded during the recording, potentially exposing personal details, passwords, payment-card data, or other confidential information. Sensitive content should be removed before the HAR file is submitted, and access should be limited to the authorized support representative.

**Learn more:** [Before you contact Chrome Enterprise support](https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/9293135?hl=en-GB)

options.text: Enable Search Ads 360 at the top level of your organizational structure.

Enable Search Ads 360 for the marketing organizational unit (OU). Create a new group in the Admin console that includes the web design team users who need access. Enable Search Ads 360 for that group.

Enable Search Ads 360 for both the marketing and web design team organizational units (OUs). Create a group to explicitly deny access to Search Ads 360. Assign the group to the web design users who should not have access.
Enable Search Ads 360 for the marketing organizational unit (OU). Create a sub-OU under the marketing OU. and move the web design team users who need access into this sub-OU.

questions.explanation:
Google Admin console service controls support enabling Search Ads 360 for an organizational unit and for an access group. Assigning the marketing OU enables the service for that department, while an access group grants it only to the designated web design users, leaving all other users without access.

**Learn more:** [Turn Search Ads 360 on or off for users](https://support.google.com/a/answer/15203902?hl=en)

You are setting up Gmail for your company and want to use a layered security approach. You decide to deploy industry-standard email-authentication protocols. What should you do? (Choose two.)

options.text: Disable IMAP for your organization to prevent external clients from accessing Gmail
Set up SPF records to specify authorized mail servers for your domain
Configure DKIM to digitally sign outbound emails and verify their origin
Configure a blocked senders rule to block all emails from unknown senders
Enable a default email quarantine for all users to isolate suspicious emails and determine if the messages haven't been authenticated.

questions.explanation:
SPF authorizes the mail servers permitted to send email for a domain through a DNS record. DKIM adds a cryptographic signature to outbound email that receiving servers use with the domain’s public key to authenticate the message and help protect the domain from spoofing.

**Learn more:** [Set up SPF — Google Workspace Admin Help](https://support.google.com/a/answer/33786) · [Set up DKIM — Google Workspace Admin Help](https://support.google.com/a/answer/174124)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization wants to give a select group of users access to YouTube for educational purposes while restricting YouTube access for all other users. You need to implement a solution that provides granular control of YouTube access according to user roles or groups. What should you do?

options.text: Configure a SAML application to manage YouTube access for different user groups
Deploy a Chrome extension from the Google Workspace Marketplace that blocks YouTube for users who are not in the select user group.
Use organizational units (OUs) to apply a policy that restricts YouTube access and create an exception for the select group of users.
Instruct the select group of users to switch to their personal Google account when accessing YouTube.

questions.explanation:
Google Workspace YouTube permissions can be applied to organizational units and overridden for a specific organizational unit or configuration group. Restricting YouTube for the general population and applying an exception to the organizational unit containing the selected users provides centralized, granular access control.

**Learn more:** [Give certain users unrestricted YouTube access](https://support.google.com/edu/setup/answer/6208228?hl=en)

Your organization uses Gmail, while the banks use a variety of other email providers. You need to maximize privacy and restrict access to messages sent and received between your organization and the banks. What should you do?

options.text: Set up Transport Layer Security (TLS) compliance for inbound and outbound messages with a list of the banks’ email domains. Validate the TLS connections.
Configure Sender Policy Framework (SPF) and DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) authentication for your email domains.
Enable Protect against unauthenticated emails in Gmail Safety.
Enable confidential mode for Gmail. Instruct employees to use confidential mode when sending messages to the banks.

questions.explanation:
Gmail TLS compliance can enforce secure TLS delivery for mail sent to and received from specified bank domains. If a specified domain cannot support TLS, Gmail rejects inbound mail or does not send outbound mail, preventing those messages from being exchanged over an unencrypted connection. SPF and DKIM authenticate senders rather than encrypting message transport, and confidential mode does not provide the same bidirectional transport enforcement.

**Learn more:** [Email routing and delivery options for Google Workspace](https://support.google.com/a/answer/2685650?hl=en-to) · [Ciphers for Gmail SMTP TLS connections](https://support.google.com/a/answer/9795993?hl=en-CA)

You must ensure that Gemini features are available only to users in the marketing and sales departments by using the most efficient approach. What should you do?

options.text: Create a script to assign a Gemini license to new users if they are in marketing or sales. Run the script daily.
Create an organizational unit (OU) for marketing and sales. Assign the Gemini licenses to that OU, and enable Gemini for that OU only.
Assign Gemini licenses to each user in the marketing and sales departments.
Enable Gemini for the entire organization. Instruct users in other departments not to use Gemini.

questions.explanation:
Google Workspace administrators can assign licenses to an organizational unit and apply Gemini user-access settings to that organizational unit. A marketing-and-sales OU therefore provides centralized, automatic scope for both the Gemini licenses and enabled Gemini service, while keeping the feature unavailable to other departments.

**Learn more:** [Assign, remove, and reassign licenses](https://support.google.com/a/answer/1727173) · [Turn the Gemini app on or off - Business / Enterprise](https://support.google.com/a/answer/14571493)

Your company manages sensitive client data and must maintain a high level of security to comply with strict industry regulations. You need to enable the company’s security team to investigate possible security breaches by using the security investigation tool in the Google Admin console.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create an activity rule that triggers email notifications to the security team whenever a high-risk security event occurs.
Assign the User Management Admin role to the security team.
Assign the super admin role to the security team
Create an administrator role with Security Center access. Assign the role to the security team.

questions.explanation:
The security investigation tool requires the Security Center administrator privilege. A custom administrator role with Security Center access gives the security team the required investigation capability while following least privilege, rather than granting unrestricted super administrator permissions.

**Learn more:** [Admin privileges for the security center](https://support.google.com/cloudidentity/answer/7532105?hl=en) · [Administrator privilege definitions](https://support.google.com/a/answer/1219251?hl=en)

questions.domain: Managing security policies and access controls
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to provide a specified group of users in your company with access to YouTube while restricting their access to Merchant Center. What should you do?

options.text: Enable YouTube for all users in the company. Individually restrict access to Merchant Center for specific Groups or organizational units (OUs).
Create YouTube and Merchant Center as custom web apps. Apply access policies at the Group or organizational unit (OU) level.
Contact Google Support and request that they enable YouTube access for the specific set of users and restrict their access to Merchant Center.
Enable access to YouTube at the Group or organizational unit (OU) level for the subset of users. Disable access to Merchant Center.

questions.explanation:
Google Workspace service-status controls allow YouTube to be enabled for a selected group or organizational unit, while Merchant Center can be disabled to prevent its use. This provides the required targeted YouTube access and Merchant Center restriction through the Admin console.

**Learn more:** [Turn a service on or off for Google Workspace users](https://support.google.com/a/answer/10628768?hl=en) · [Turn Merchant Center on or off for users](https://support.google.com/a/answer/15202792?hl=en)

questions.domain: Managing security policies and access controls
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company wants to reduce distractions and inappropriate content in its Google Chat spaces. You need to enable trusted employees to delete messages and ban users from particular Chat spaces. What should you do?

options.text: Assign the trusted employees as moderators for the relevant Chat spaces.
Create a data loss prevention (DLP) rule that blocks inappropriate content from being shared
Use the security investigation tool to audit and monitor Chat messages.
Disable all Chat spaces except those specifically approved by management.

questions.explanation:
Google Chat space-level moderation roles provide the authority to remove participants and delete messages in the relevant spaces. Google documents that space owners and managers can remove members, and that they can delete any message in a space; assigning trusted employees the corresponding moderation role meets both requirements.

**Learn more:** [Learn about your role as a space owner or manager — Google Chat Help](https://support.google.com/chat/answer/11833441?co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop&hl=en) · [Manage space settings — Google Chat Help](https://support.google.com/chat/answer/13340792?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Users at your company report that they are not receiving certain emails in their corporate Gmail accounts. You checked the Google Workspace Status Dashboard and found no service disruptions. You need to determine the root cause and resolve the mail-delivery issues. What should you do? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use Email Log Search (ELS) to identify specific delivery failures.
Verify whether the organization’s Mail Exchange (MX) records are correctly configured.
Check the users’ spam folders to determine whether emails are being misdirected.
Investigate the Gmail log events for error messages or unusual patterns.
Check the senders’ IP addresses in the inbound mail gateway.

questions.explanation:
Google Workspace MX records must point to Google mail servers for the domain to receive email. Email Log Search traces specific expected messages and exposes delivery outcomes, including messages routed incorrectly or marked as spam, enabling targeted mail-delivery troubleshooting.

**Learn more:** [Troubleshoot problems receiving emails in Gmail](https://support.google.com/a/answer/11112228?hl=en) · [Troubleshoot message delivery with Email Log Search](https://support.google.com/a/answer/7513679?hl=en)

questions.domain: Managing security policies and access controls
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An increase in phishing emails includes links to malicious files hosted on external Google Drives. These files often impersonate legitimate documents and deceive users into granting access to their accounts.  
  
You need to stop users from accessing these malicious external Drive files while still allowing access to legitimate external files. What should you do? (Choose two.)

options.text: Enforce stricter password policies.
Conduct regular security awareness training to educate users.
Create a Drive trust rule that blocks all external domains except for a pre-approved list of trusted partners.
Deploy advanced malware detection software on all user devices to scan and block malicious files.
Implement two-factor authentication for all users.

questions.explanation:
Drive trust rules can restrict which external users or domains may share files with internal users, allowing collaboration with approved partners while blocking untrusted sources. Regular security-awareness training helps users identify phishing links, impersonated documents, and deceptive access-consent requests before they grant account access.

**Learn more:** [Create and manage trust rules for Drive sharing](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/security/create-and-manage-trust-rules-for-drive-sharing?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company runs several primary care clinics in which employees routinely handle protected health information (PHI). The organization is transitioning from a legacy communication and collaboration system to Google Workspace. After signing the Business Associate Agreement (BAA), what should you do to ensure that data is handled in compliance with regulations when using Google Workspace?

options.text: Implement a third-party backup service that is also compliant with Google Workspace core services.
Create a label for Google Drive content to help employees identify sensitive data.
Instruct the staff to not store any PHI in Google Workspace core services, including Google Drive, Docs, Sheets, and Keep.
Disable integrations with third-party apps and turn off non-core Google services.

questions.explanation:
PHI is permitted in specific Google Workspace services covered as HIPAA Included Functionality after a BAA is in place, including Google Drive, Docs, Sheets, and Keep. Third-party applications and add-ons are not covered by Google’s BAA, and non-core Google services must be disabled for users who manage PHI unless a separate BAA covers them.

**Learn more:** [HIPAA Compliance with Google Workspace and Cloud Identity](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/compliance/hipaa-compliance-with-google-workspace-and-cloud-identity?hl=en) · [Google Workspace and Cloud Identity HIPAA Implementation Guide](https://services.google.com/fh/files/misc/gsuite_cloud_identity_hipaa_implementation_guide.pdf)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for a large organization that does not allow employees to use Google Sites. However, a task force of three people from each of five different departments has recently been established to work on a project assigned by the Office of the CIO. You must temporarily allow the users in this task force to use Google Sites. You want the least disruptive and most efficient approach. What should you do?

options.text: Turn Google Sites access on for each of the 15 users in the task force.
Create a configuration group for the task force’s 15 users. Grant Google Sites access to the group.
Place the 15 task force users into a new organizational unit (OU). Turn on Google Sites access for the OU.
Create an access group for the task force’s 15 users. Grant Google Sites access to the group.

questions.explanation:
Google Workspace access groups allow a service to be enabled for a selected set of users across organizational units. Creating an access group for the 15 task-force members and enabling Google Sites for that group grants the temporary exception without moving users from their existing OUs or changing access one user at a time.

**Learn more:** [Turn Sites on or off for users — Google Workspace Admin Help](https://support.google.com/a/answer/9974997?hl=en)

Several employees in your finance department are working together on a long-term, multi-phase project. You need to quickly create a confidential group for this project while minimizing management overhead. What should you do?

options.text: Create a Google Group by using Google Cloud Directory Sync (GCDS) to automatically sync the members.
Create a dynamic group and define the Department user attribute as a condition for membership with the value as the finance department.
Create a Google Group and update the settings to allow anyone in the organization to join the group.
Create a Google Group and appoint a group admin to manage the membership of this group.

questions.explanation:
A standard Google Group can limit membership to the specific project participants and remain confidential. Assigning a group manager delegates membership administration; managers can manage members and group settings, reducing ongoing administrative overhead for the group owner.

**Learn more:** [Create a group and choose group settings](https://support.google.com/groups/answer/2464926?hl=en) · [Manage membership automatically with dynamic groups](https://support.google.com/cloudidentity/answer/10286834?hl=en-uk)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company’s help desk is getting technical-support tickets from employees who say that messages from known external contacts are being routed to the **Spam** label in Gmail. You need to resolve the issue and ensure legitimate emails are delivered without adding risk, as quickly as possible. What should you do?

options.text: Ask employees to select the messages in Gmail that are being delivered to spam and mark them as Not spam.
Contact the external senders, and tell them to authenticate their sent mail by using domain-based message authentication, reporting, and conformance (DMARC).
Turn off more aggressive spam filtering in spam policies that are applied to the users’ organizational unit and add the senders’ mail system IP addresses to the email allowlist.
Create an address list of approved senders so messages from these users bypass Gmail’s spam filters and recipients can decide whether they are spam or not.

questions.explanation:
An approved senders address list identifies trusted email addresses or domains whose messages bypass Gmail’s spam filters, while allowing recipients to decide whether a message is spam. This restores delivery for legitimate known contacts without disabling broader anti-spam protections or allowlisting potentially changing mail-system IP addresses.

**Learn more:** [Allowlists, denylists, and approved senders](https://support.google.com/a/answer/60752?hl=en)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An employee at your company who has a Workspace Business Plus license will soon begin a long leave. The employee will not require access to their Google Workspace data, but their teammates will need access to that employee’s data. When the employee returns from leave, you must restore access to their account, data, emails, and shared documents.  
  
You need to retain the employee’s Workspace data while minimizing costs during the leave. What should you do?

options.text: Suspend their account in the Admin console.
Purchase an Archived User license and assign the license to the employee.
Export the account data by using Takeout, and remove the user license in the Admin console.
Copy the employee's emails, and transfer their file ownership to a teammate. Delete the user account.

questions.explanation:
A Business Plus Archived User license preserves the user’s Google Workspace services data while blocking the user from signing in, and it makes the active Google Workspace license available for reassignment. The archived account can later be unarchived and restored to active use, retaining its Gmail, Drive data, and shared-document relationships. Suspending an account preserves data but continues billing for the active user license.

**Learn more:** [Add Archived User licenses](https://support.google.com/a/answer/9048232) · [Google Workspace setup FAQ](https://support.google.com/a/answer/6142901)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are applying device and user policies for employees in different departments in your organization. Each department requires a distinct set of policies. To follow Google-recommended practices, what should you do?

options.text: Add all managed users and devices in the top-level organizational unit.
Create an Access group for each department Configure the applicable policies.
Create a child organizational unit for each department.
Create separate top-level organizational units for each department.

questions.explanation:
Child organizational units let administrators apply distinct user and device policies to each department while inheriting applicable settings from the top-level organization. Google documentation identifies organizational units as the mechanism for controlling settings by department; access groups are intended for granting service access across or within departments rather than structuring department-specific policies.

**Learn more:** [Move users to an organizational unit](https://support.google.com/a/answer/182449?hl=en-na) · [Turn Sites on or off for users](https://support.google.com/a/answer/9974997?hl=en-419)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],The current storage limit for the sales organizational unit (OU) at your company is 10GB per user. A subset of sales representatives in that OU requires 100GB of storage across shared services. You must increase storage for only that subset of sales representatives using the least disruptive approach and the fewest configuration steps. What should you do?

options.text: Move the subset of users to a sub-OU, and assign a 100GB storage limit to that sub-OU.
Instruct the subset of users to store their documents in a Shared Drive with a 100GB limit.
Change the storage limit of the sales OU to 100GB.
Create a configuration group, and add the subset of users to that group. Set the group storage limit to 100GB.

questions.explanation:
Google Workspace lets administrators apply a per-user storage limit to a configuration group. Group storage limits override organizational-unit storage limits for the group’s members, so the selected sales representatives can receive a 100GB limit while remaining in the sales OU and other users keep the 10GB limit.

**Learn more:** [Set storage limits for users](https://support.google.com/a/answer/12002975)

questions.domain: Managing security policies and access controls
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],The innovation team at your organization has a dedicated room containing prototype equipment. You need to make the room reservable, add the equipment, and ensure no booking conflicts occur. Only the innovation team and the sales directors may access this room. What should you do?

options.text: Create a separate Google Calendar resource for the room. Manually manage booking requests from both teams.
Create a Google Group for the innovation team and another Google Group for sales directors. Share the room’s calendar with both groups.
Create a Google Calendar event for the room. Share the event with the innovation team and sales directors.
Edit the Google Calendar settings for the room resource. Adjust the permission settings so only the innovation team and sales director group can view and book time on this calendar.

questions.explanation:
Google Calendar resources are designed for shared rooms and equipment. A resource has its own calendar and can be configured for booking, including automatic handling of invitations to avoid conflicting reservations. Restricting the resource calendar’s permissions to the innovation team and the sales directors allows only those groups to view availability and reserve the room.

**Learn more:** [Create buildings, features & Calendar resources](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/calendar/create-buildings-features-and-calendar-resources) · [Share room and resource calendars](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/calendar/share-room-and-resource-calendars)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to create an automated application or process that includes connectors to external data, uses Google Sheets data, and can be easily shared as a mobile application. What should you do?

options.text: Create an application by using App Engine. Connect the application to your Workspace environment
Copy the external data to BigQuery. Use a Connected Sheet to interact with the data.
Create an AppSheet application to connect the different data sources. Set up the mobile application.
Create an automation process by using Apps Script. Run the process through Google Sheets.

questions.explanation:
AppSheet can build mobile apps that use Google Sheets as a data source and combine it with other data sources or connectors. AppSheet apps are supported on iOS and Android devices, making it the appropriate integrated solution for external data, Sheets data, and mobile sharing.

**Learn more:** [Manage data sources — AppSheet Help](https://support.google.com/appsheet/answer/10106309?hl=en) · [Support for AppSheet apps on mobile devices and browsers — AppSheet Help](https://support.google.com/appsheet/answer/10105385?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company recently installed a free email-marketing platform from the Google Workspace Marketplace. options.text: Use the security investigation tool to review Gmail logs.
Confirm that the
Check the OAuth scopes that are granted to the email marketing platform and ensure the platform has access to Contacts and Gmail.
Verify that the email marketing platform's subscription is active and up-to-date.

questions.explanation:
