**Learn more:** [Control which apps access Google Workspace data](https://support.google.com/a/answer/7281227?hl=en&p=app_access_apps)

questions.domain: Managing security policies and access controls
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Employees in your organization often collaborate with external clients and vendors through Google Meet. Your organization has active unsupervised meetings with no host, as well as unsupervised meetings that remain active after an event has ended. You need to end all meetings being used inappropriately as quickly as possible. What should you do?

options.text: End all unsupervised meetings by using the Google Meet APIs.
Enable Host Management for Google Meet, and train internal host employees how to end meetings for everyone.
Turn off Google Meet in the Admin console for your organization. Turn Google Meet back on after two minutes.
Identify and end all unsupervised meetings by using the security investigation tool.

questions.explanation:
The security investigation tool lets an authorized Google Workspace administrator search Meet log events, identify selected active or old improperly used meetings, and apply **End meeting for all**. This action removes current participants and prevents future instances from being joined without a host, directly addressing unsupervised meetings with no host and meetings that continue after an event.

**Learn more:** [Use the security investigation tool to end meetings](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/security/use-the-security-investigation-tool-to-end-meetings?rd=1&visit_id=639176419926010119-3407717645)

questions.question: You are planning a group structure for your company to grant access to a particular shared drive. The solution must automatically add and remove employees according to their job role. What should you do?

options.text: Create a security group. Add all employees with the desired job role. Grant the security group access to the shared drive.
Create a distribution list. Add all employees with the desired job role. Grant the distribution list access to the shared drive.
Create a dynamic group. Set the membership criteria to the desired job role. Grant the dynamic group access to the shared drive.
Create a configuration group. Add users on an exception basis. Grant the configuration group access to the shared drive.

questions.explanation: A dynamic group uses membership criteria based on user attributes, such as job role, so its membership updates automatically as those attributes change. The group can then be granted access to the shared drive.

options.text: Change the Chrome Web Store allow/block mode setting to allow all apps, admin manages blocklist, In the App access control card, block any existing web app that is not on the security team’s vetted list.

questions.explanation:

Adding the security team’s vetted items to that allowlist blocks all unapproved items by default, satisfying both the existing-installation and future-installation restrictions.

options.text: Create the templates in Google Drive. Grant edit access to the sales team.
Create the templates in Google Drive and download the files as PDFs. Upload PDF files to a drive shared with your sales team.
Create the templates in Google Drive. Make a copy for each sales representative Transfer ownership of each template to the sales representatives.

Enable visitor sharing for the organizational unit (OU) in your Workspace domain.

questions.explanation:

You are setting up email for your company’s Google Workspace account. The company wants to stop certain file types from being sent or received as email attachments in the simplest, most cost-effective manner. What should you do?

options.text: Adjust the maximum message size limit to prevent large files from being sent or received.
Enable the Security Sandbox in Gmail to automatically quarantine emails with suspicious attachments.
Scan all incoming and outgoing emails for malicious attachments by using an industry standard third-party email security solution.
Configure an attachment compliance rule in Gmail settings to block specific file types.

questions.explanation:
Gmail attachment compliance rules can match specified attachment file types and block or reject matching messages for the relevant inbound and outbound mail flow. This is a built-in Google Workspace administrative control, so it directly enforces a file-type restriction without requiring a third-party email-security product.

**Learn more:** [Filter messages with attachments | Gmail | Google Workspace Help](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/gmail/advanced/filter-messages-with-attachments?hl=en)

options.text: Create a Google Group for each region and add the respective employees to the appropriate group.

Your company’s security team must be able to investigate unauthorized external file sharing. You need to ensure the security team can use the security investigation tool while following the principle of least privilege. What should you do?

options.text: Grant the super admin role to a delegate from the security team.
Create a pre-built reporting role. Assign the role to the security team alias.
Share the Drive audit log with the security team.
Create a custom admin role with security center privileges. Assign the role to the individual security team members.

questions.explanation:
Access to the security investigation tool is controlled through Security Center administrator privileges. A custom administrator role can grant the specific Security Center privileges required for investigation to the individual security team members, without assigning the broad super administrator role.

**Learn more:** [Admin privileges for the security center](https://support.google.com/cloudidentity/answer/7532105?hl=en) · [Administrator privilege definitions](https://support.google.com/a/answer/1219251?hl=en-uk)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You must ensure that data owned by former employees remains available in Google Vault. You want to use the most cost-effective option.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Migrate the former employees’ Gmail to their manager(s) by using the data migration service during the deletion process. Transfer the former employees’ Google Drive files to a new owner.
Change the Google account passwords of the former employees.
Suspend the former employees’ Google accounts. Create an organizational unit (OU). Move the former employees into that OU.
Assign an Archived User license to the former employees’ Google accounts.

questions.explanation:
An Archived User license keeps a former employee’s Google Workspace data available for Google Vault retention, holds, and searches without maintaining an active account. Suspended accounts are billed at the same rate as active accounts, so Archived User licensing is the cost-effective preservation option.

**Learn more:** [Preserve data for users who leave your organization](https://support.google.com/vault/answer/2736622?hl=en) · [Google Vault FAQ](https://support.google.com/vault/answer/2539616?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Users in your organization report that Gmail is incorrectly identifying a high volume of legitimate emails as spam. You want to troubleshoot the issue while following Google-recommended practices. What should you do?

options.text: Adjust the organization’s mail content compliance settings in the Admin console.
Advise users to individually allowlist senders.
Disable spam filtering for all users.
Contact Google Workspace support and report a suspected system-wide spam filter malfunction.

questions.explanation:
A widespread pattern of legitimate messages being classified as spam warrants escalation to Google Workspace support for investigation of a possible system-wide spam-filtering problem. Disabling spam filtering or relying on individual sender allowlists weakens protection and does not address a broad service-level cause. Google Workspace administrators can contact Google support directly for product issues.

questions.question: Your organization is migrating its existing on-premises email solution to Google Workspace. You need to ensure that email sent to your domain is properly routed to Gmail. What should you do?

options.text: Change the Mail Exchange (MX) records in your current email domain’s DNS settings to point to Google’s mail servers.
Set up email forwarding from your on-premises email provider to Gmail.
Create a content compliance rule to filter and route incoming emails.
Configure SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records in your current email domain’s DNS settings.

questions.explanation:
MX records tell sending mail systems which servers accept email for a domain. Updating the domain’s DNS MX records to Google’s mail servers directs inbound messages to Gmail. SPF, DKIM, and DMARC support email authentication and anti-spoofing, but they do not specify inbound mail routing.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set up MX records for Google Workspace](https://support.google.com/a/answer/6156494)

options.text: Verify that the audio drivers on the affected laptops are up-to-date and functioning correctly.
Check the Admin console to determine whether there are recent Meet-related notifications or alerts.
Check if Context-Aware access rules were set to prevent Meet access from the user’s network location.

questions.explanation:

This directly pinpoints where the audio failed for the affected employees without touching each laptop. Checking audio drivers on every laptop (A) is slow, generic Meet alerts (B) will not localize a per-user audio issue, and Context-Aware access (C) would block Meet entirely rather than degrade audio.

questions.explanation:

questions.domain: Managing security policies and access controls
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],External sharing in your company is permitted only for the sales and marketing department. Engineering must not share externally. You need to configure sharing settings to meet this policy. What should you do?

options.text: Use a data loss prevention (DLP) solution to control external sharing based on user groups.
Create separate shared drives for each department with different external sharing settings.
Create organizational units (OUs) for each department. Configure different external sharing settings for each OU.
Configure Drive trust rules to restrict the engineering department from sharing externally.

questions.explanation:
Google Drive external-sharing settings can be applied to an organizational unit, which is commonly used for departments. Separate organizational units allow sales and marketing to have external sharing enabled while engineering has it disabled, covering the users’ Drive sharing policy by department.

questions.question: You administer Chrome Enterprise browsers for a large organization. You need to ensure that particular extensions are installed automatically on every managed Chrome Enterprise browser. What should you do?

options.text: Allowlist the specific Chrome browser extensions.
Configure a script to deploy the extensions upon user login.
Publish the extensions in the Chrome Web Store.
Force-install the extensions through Chrome browser policies.

questions.explanation:
The Chrome Enterprise ExtensionInstallForcelist policy force-installs specified extensions silently and without user interaction. It is the enterprise policy mechanism for mandatory extension deployment across managed browsers.\

options.text: Use a third-party mobile device management (MDM) solution to manage the device.
Allow the employee to use their personal device without enrolling it in any mobile device management (MDM) solution.
Implement Google’s basic management solution for the mobile device.
Implement Google’s advanced management solution for the mobile device.

questions.explanation:
Google Workspace advanced mobile management enforces security policies through a management client and offers greater control over Android devices than basic management. Use the security investigation tool to search user log events for
Verify whether users in the affected buildings have been assigned Google Voice licenses.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An organization has a Shared Drive with 150 users organized in a group. Every group member must be able to add and edit files, while the ability to move, delete, and share content must be restricted to one user. You need to configure the shared drive efficiently to satisfy these requirements.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create a folder inside the shared drive. Share the files with the group by using the share function.
Create a folder inside the shared drive. Share the folder link with the group.
In the Admin console, assign Contributor access for the shared drive to each user. Assign Content Manager access for the shared drive to the single user.
In the Admin console, assign Contributor access for the shared drive to the group. Assign Content Manager access for the shared drive to the single user.

questions.explanation:
Assigning access to the group avoids maintaining 150 individual memberships. Contributor access permits members to create, upload, and edit files but does not permit them to move files or folders within the shared drive or move them to the Trash. Content Manager access gives the designated user the elevated ability to move and delete content. Where sharing must be restricted beyond the role’s default permissions, shared-drive sharing settings must also prevent Contributors from sharing individual files.

**Learn more:** [How file access works in shared drives](https://support.google.com/a/users/answer/12380484?hl=en) · [Store & share files or folders with shared drives](https://support.google.com/drive/answer/7286514?co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop&hl=en-en-16)

questions.domain: Managing security policies and access controls
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization is concerned about attempts at unauthorized access. You want to implement a security measure that requires users to change their password when there are twenty or more failed sign-in attempts within one hour. You want to use the most effective and efficient method. What should you do?

options.text: Set up a Chrome action rule to restrict users from defined ChromeOS actions after twenty failed password attempts.
Create an activity rule for user log events, define a time period and threshold, and select an Action for the rule to force a password change.
Create an activity rule for live-state data sources that meets the required time period and threshold to identify users who need to change their password.
Enable email alerts to notify users that they need to change their password.

questions.explanation:
Google Workspace activity rules support User log events, event-frequency thresholds over a defined time period, and automated actions such as forcing a password change. Activity rules cannot be created from live-state data sources; email alerts only notify recipients and do not enforce the password change.

**Learn more:** [Create and manage activity rules — Google Workspace Admin Help](https://support.google.com/a/answer/9275024?hl=en-419)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for a healthcare provider that uses an external medical billing company to manage patient records and invoices. options.text: Create a shared drive that is managed by your organization’s employees. Grant Contributor access to the billing company’s staff.
Create a shared drive. Grant Content Manager access to your organization’s employees and the billing company.
Create a group, and add the employees from your organization and the billing company. Create a shared folder on Google Drive. Grant Editor access to the group
Restrict access for the medical billing company’s employees by using Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies.

questions.domain: Managing security policies and access controls
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization has identified a substantial increase in unauthorized access to applications from personal devices. This creates a critical security risk and may result in data loss. To reduce this risk, you must immediately restrict users' access to these applications. What should you do?

options.text: Enable data loss prevention rules.
Limit apps access to company-issued devices by using context-aware access.
Configure apps data access to Limited to only allow access to unrestricted services.
Enable multi-factor authentication for application access.

questions.explanation:
Context-Aware Access supports granular application-access policies based on device context, including device security status and company ownership. Requiring a company-owned device blocks access from personal devices while allowing authorized users to continue accessing the applications from organization-issued devices.

**Learn more:** [About Context-Aware Access — Google Workspace Admin Help](https://support.google.com/a/answer/12645308) · [About Android device management with Google endpoint management — Google Workspace Admin Help](https://support.google.com/a/answer/12010750)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You observe an increase in Gmail-related support tickets. Several users report that their email is not loading and that they are seeing error messages. You need to troubleshoot the problem and identify possible causes. What should you do?

options.text: Review the users' email forwarding settings to ensure that emails are not being redirected to incorrect addresses.
Analyze the users' Gmail labels and filters to determine whether incoming emails are being inadvertently blocked.
Gather HAR files from affected users to capture network traffic and analyze request/response details.
Collect the users' browser versions and extensions to identify potential compatibility issues.

questions.explanation: A HAR file captures the browser’s network requests and responses while the failure is reproduced, enabling investigation of failed HTTP requests, server responses, authentication or proxy problems, and other network-related causes of Gmail loading errors. Email forwarding, labels, and filters do not ordinarily prevent the Gmail interface from loading.

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],The company’s legal department has issued a litigation hold requiring preservation of all data connected to a particular project. You must ensure that all project data—including emails, documents, and chats—is retained indefinitely and cannot be deleted by users. What should you do?

options.text: Create a hold in Google Vault that includes all users and data sources associated with the project.
Assign an Archived User license to all users involved in the project.
Set up a retention rule in Google Vault that retains all data from Gmail and Drive indefinitely.
Export all project related data from Google Workspace and store the data in a separate, secure location.

questions.explanation:
Google Vault holds are designed for legal preservation. A hold can be scoped to the relevant custodians and services, including Gmail, Drive, and on-the-record Google Chat, and preserves covered data indefinitely until the hold is removed. Holds override retention rules, so user-deleted covered data remains available in Vault.

**Learn more:** [Get started with holds in Google Vault](https://support.google.com/vault/answer/7664657?hl=en) · [Manage retention rules and holds](https://support.google.com/vault/answer/3374023?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A group of temporary employees departed the organization after finishing a shared project. Under company policy, their Google Workspace accounts must be disabled while all project data and associated communications are retained in Google Vault for at least two years. You need to meet this policy at the lowest possible cost. What should you do?

options.text: Purchase and assign Archived User licenses to the former employees.
Transfer the former employees’ files and data to active user accounts. Delete the former employees’ Workspace accounts.
Purchase additional user licenses and suspend the former employees’ accounts.
Move the former employees to their own organizational unit (OU) and disable access to Google services for that OU.

questions.explanation:
An Archived User license preserves a former employee’s Google Workspace data so it remains available to Google Vault while the user cannot access Workspace services. Deleting the account also deletes its Workspace data, including data retained by Vault, and suspended accounts are billed at the same rate as active accounts. Vault retention rules can retain the preserved data for the required two-year period.

**Learn more:** [Preserve data for users who leave your organization](https://support.google.com/vault/answer/2736622?hl=en) · [How retention works](https://support.google.com/vault/answer/2990828?hl=en)

options.text: Configure the allowed list of apps in the Devices page in the apps and extensions settings.
Configure the Chrome user setting to require users to sign in to use Chrome apps and extensions.
Configure the Policy Precedence to override the domain-wide policy applied for apps and extensions.
Require 2SV for user logins.

questions.explanation:
Chrome policies configured for enrolled browsers/devices apply when Chrome opens on the managed device, without requiring a user to sign in. Those device-level policies are appropriate for enforcing security restrictions such as allowed or blocked apps and extensions.

**Learn more:** [Set Chrome policies for users or browsers](https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/2657289?hl=en)

Your company is simplifying workflows by creating custom applications for tasks such as submitting expense reports or requesting time off. You need to identify a Google Workspace solution for developing these applications. Your development team has only basic coding knowledge. What should you do?

options.text: Enable AppSheet for your organization.
Enable Gemini for Workspace. Direct users to use generative Al across Gmail and Drive to simplify the submission of expense reports.
Enable AppScript for your organization and allow employees to build add-ons to existing Workspace solutions.
Direct employees to use Google Forms to collect data and create basic workflows.

questions.explanation:
AppSheet is a no-code application development platform that enables business users and IT teams to create and customize workflow applications through an interactive interface, making it suitable for expense-report and time-off-request apps without substantial programming expertise.

**Learn more:** [Get started with AppSheet](https://support.google.com/appsheet/answer/11581986?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A user in your organization received a spam email and reported it for further investigation. You need to quickly determine additional details and the scope of this incident. What should you do?

options.text: Conduct a Vault search to find this email and identify if additional users were affected.
Conduct a search to find all emails sent by the sender by using the Gmail API.
Conduct an Email reports search to find this email and all of the email’s recipients.
Conduct a search in the security investigation tool to find this email, and identify whether additional users were affected.

questions.explanation:
The security investigation tool can search Gmail message data across the organization using attributes such as message ID, sender, recipients, and content. This enables investigation of the reported message and identification of other users who received or were affected by it.

**Learn more:** [Gmail messages — Google Workspace Help](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/security/gmail-messages?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are setting up data-governance policies for your organization’s Google Drive. You must ensure that employees in the Research and Development department can share files with external users, while employees in the Finance department are prevented from sharing any files externally. What should you do?

options.text: Create a Drive trust rule that allows external sharing for the Research and Development organizational unit (OU) and another rule that blocks external sharing for the Finance OU.
Apply an organization-wide data loss prevention (DLP) rule that scans for sensitive information and prevents external sharing of those files. Apply that rule to the Finance organizational unit (OU).
Create a separate Google Workspace domain for the Finance organizational unit (OU) and disable external sharing for that domain.
Enable Vault for the Finance organizational unit (OU) to ensure that all files shared externally are retained and auditable.

questions.explanation:
Google Workspace Drive sharing controls and trust rules can enforce different external-sharing permissions for organizational units. An allow rule for the Research and Development OU and a blocking rule for the Finance OU meets the departmental requirement. DLP is content-condition-based, whereas Vault provides retention and audit capabilities rather than an external-sharing prohibition.

**Learn more:** [Configure Google Drive file sharing](https://support.google.com/a/answer/9178844)

Select a mobile management solution that provides basic passcode enforcement and enables an administrator to remotely wipe a user’s account from the device. You also want to avoid installing agents on employees’ personal devices. What should you do?

options.text: Implement Google’s advanced management on mobile devices.
Implement Google’s basic management on mobile devices.
Enforce a strong password policy, and enforce the password policy at the next sign-in.
Deploy a third-party mobile device management (MDM) solution.

questions.explanation:
Google basic mobile management supports basic passcode requirements and lets an administrator remotely wipe a user’s work account from a mobile device. It does not require users to install a management app or set up a work profile, making it appropriate for personal devices with limited management requirements.

**Learn more:** [Set up basic mobile device management](https://support.google.com/a/answer/7400753) · [About Android device management with Google endpoint management](https://support.google.com/a/answer/12010750)

Your organization has recently seen an increase in unauthorized attempts to access its Google Workspace instance. You need to improve user-account security while adhering to Google-recommended practices. What should you do?

options.text: Disable password recovery options to prevent unauthorized individuals from accessing user accounts.
Implement a strong password policy and enable text messages as the 2-Step Verification (2SV) using text messages.
Enforce the use of physical security keys as the 2-Step Verification (2SV) method for all users.
Enforce a strong password policy that requires users to include special characters, numbers, and uppercase letters.

questions.explanation:
Physical security keys are Google’s strongest 2-Step Verification method and protect against phishing threats, providing a possession-based factor in addition to the password. Google discourages SMS-based verification because text messages can be intercepted.

**Learn more:** [Protect your business with 2-Step Verification - Google Workspace Admin Help](https://support.google.com/a/answer/175197)

As part of the audit, you must demonstrate that you can preserve all electronic communications related to a particular project for a potential legal-discovery process. You need to configure Google Vault to meet this objective. What should you do?

options.text: Use the security investigation report to show Vault log events.
Use the search and export functionality to identify all relevant communications within the project timeframe.
Create a matter and a hold on all project-related data sources such as Email, Chat, and Drive within Google Workspace.
Create a custom retention policy for the project data. Ensure that the policy covers the required retention period.

questions.explanation:
Google Vault matters provide the workspace for an eDiscovery project, and holds preserve data for legal or investigation purposes until the hold is removed. Applying holds to the relevant project custodians or organizational units for Gmail, Chat, and Drive preserves the covered data and takes precedence over normal retention rules.

**Learn more:** [Get started with holds in Google Vault](https://support.google.com/vault/answer/7664657?hl=en) · [Create and manage matters](https://support.google.com/vault/answer/2462419?hl=en)
